question: On fresh images, does the Phase 72 'watch forensics' ensemble (fine-tuned DINOv3 + Phase 71 frozen probe + dial-text brand consistency) catch more AI-generated watch images than fine-tuned DINOv3 alone, at a comparable rate of real photos rejected?
scope_limit: Real photograph versus AI-generated image only. No physical-counterfeit or authenticity claim.
why_a_new_benchmark: benchmark_v1 images were used for the Phase 71 final test and are used to design the Phase 72 fusion rule, so they are development data now.

classes.REAL_PHOTO: Primary image of eBay listings (Browse API, category 31387, price >= 1000 USD, five brands), 60 per brand, excluding every listing and every image (SHA-256 or dHash within 2 bits) already in benchmark_v1 or in the 30,000 training images

GENERATED.kandinsky22_fresh: kandinsky-community/kandinsky-2-2-decoder, same prompt templates as v1, new seeds (base 72000), 60 per brand
GENERATED.amused512: amused/amused-512 (masked-token transformer with a VQ-GAN decoder; not a diffusion model; never used by any HypeVault model), same prompt templates, seeds base 73000, 60 per brand

normalisation: EXIF transpose, RGB, centre-crop square, Lanczos resize to exactly 512 x 512, JPEG quality 90, metadata stripped. Sources below 512 px on the short side are excluded. Every class gets the same treatment.
exclusions: Same rules as benchmark_v1 (exact SHA-256 and dHash <= 2 bits against training and within the benchmark), plus all benchmark_v1 images.
no_peeking: No model score, OCR reading or fusion output may be computed on v2 images until ml_rtx5080/experiments/watch_forensics_v1/fusion_rule.json is written and its SHA-256 recorded in v2 results. Generation and collection may happen earlier.

systems_compared.dinov3_alone: fine-tuned DINOv3 epoch_018 with its frozen benchmark policy (REVIEW gate, T = 0.2404, threshold 0.50), scored through Triton as in benchmark_v1
systems_compared.dinov2_alone: live DINOv2 with its legacy policy, for reference
systems_compared.phase71_probe: frozen DINOv3 + logistic head with its fixed threshold 0.9791
systems_compared.watch_forensics: the fusion rule frozen in fusion_rule.json

primary_analysis.generated_caught: images whose decision is FAKE, per generator group and pooled, with Clopper-Pearson 95% intervals
primary_analysis.real_rejected: real photos whose decision is FAKE, with intervals
primary_analysis.review: REVIEW counts reported separately; REVIEW is neither caught nor rejected
primary_analysis.paired: exact McNemar test, watch_forensics vs dinov3_alone, on generated images where both give a binary decision

success_criterion: watch_forensics catches more pooled generated images than dinov3_alone with McNemar p < 0.05, and its real-photo rejection rate is at most 3 percentage points above dinov3_alone's
